card.summary: Free account: maximum file size 20 GB, 2 torrents, files kept 7 days, limited download speed, limited storage size, no streaming. A guest gets 20 GB, 1 torre...

free_tier.stated: Free account: maximum file size 20 GB, 2 torrents, files kept 7 days, limited download speed, limited storage size, no streaming. A guest gets 20 GB, 1 torrent, limited speed, and nothing is stated about retention.
free_tier.notes: the vendor's own plan table; the free row is deliberately blank for several cells

per_object_cap.stated: 'Max file size 20 GB' on both Guest and Free account rows; 'Unlimited' on Premium.
per_object_cap.notes: 20 GB decimal; a 20 GiB torrent is 21.47 GB and therefore over the cap, if the vendor means GB and not GiB

retention.stated: 'Files kept for 7 days' on the free account; the guest row is blank; Premium is 'Unlimited'.

egress.terms: Free is 'Download speed Limited' with no number; Premium is 'Download speed Unlimited'. No byte allowance is stated on any row.

record.interface_detail: HTTPS download from the 'My Files' page; no API is documented anywhere on the site, only a browser UI and a browser extension.
record.tooling: browser only; no API, no CLI, no rclone backend. A wrapper would have to drive the web session.
record.chaining: the account-free guest route makes it the fastest way to test whether a 20 GB torrent is fetchable at all, before paying anyone; the 7-day retention rules it out as storage.

limits.value: 20 GB per torrent on guest and free accounts
2 torrents at once on a free account, 1 as a guest
free files are removed after 7 days

record.limits_note: the vendor publishes no byte quota and no API rate limit; older reviews report a 150 KB/s free speed cap and a 1 GB free file limit, both contradicted by the current plan table, which was read.
record.binding_note: A 20 GiB torrent sits just above the 20 GB free cap, so the size check is what fails first, before the 7-day clock or the two-torrent slot count.

identity_cost.detail: guest use needs nothing: 'ZbigZ can be used absolutely free and without registrations.' A free account is an email and password.

record.reliability_note: the plan table leaves storage size and guest retention blank, and the site's numbers have changed without any changelog; the interface is dated and there is no support channel named.
record.confidence_note: the plan comparison table was read on the mobile payment page, which is the only page carrying it (zbigz.com/payment renders only a headline). The 20 GB versus 20 GiB boundary is untested.

evidence.proved: the Guest / Free account / Premium table: 'Max file size 20 GB | 20 GB | Unlimited', 'Number of torrents 1 | 2 | Unlimited', 'Files kept for - | 7 days | Unlimited'
'ZbigZ can be used absolutely free and without registrations. No actions required.'
reported: premium is unlimited storage and unlimited file size at about $9.99/month; the older 1 GB free cap is contradicted by the vendor table

record.price_per_tb_month: free tier; premium price not published on the page read
record.notes: The one free tier among debrid providers whose published per-file cap (20 GB) is within a few percent of the 20 GiB case, and the only one usable with no account at all. Whether a 21.47 GB torrent is rejected depends on GB versus GiB, which the vendor does not say.
